flags.title: Unstable or stable angina?
flags.concern: Three months of exertional pressure that occurs with walking and is absent at rest fits stable angina; if the pain is truly unstable, a cardiology visit and stress test next week would not match the urgency.
flags.consider: You might clarify whether the pattern is new, crescendo or at rest, and if so consider same-day evaluation with troponin rather than outpatient stress testing.

evidence.quote: it mainly happens when i'm walking
my suspicion is you have something called unstable angina
we will try to get you into cardiology the next week

flags.title: Statin for diabetes and suspected CAD?
flags.concern: A 53-year-old with diabetes and suspected coronary disease would typically qualify for statin therapy, but lipids and a statin were not discussed.
flags.consider: Consider checking a lipid panel and starting a high-intensity statin alongside aspirin.

evidence.quote: past medical history of diabetes and high blood pressure
i am worried that you may have some sort of a blockage going on

flags.title: Hydrochlorothiazide first-line in a diabetic patient?
flags.concern: In diabetes an ACE inhibitor or ARB is often preferred, thiazides can worsen glycemic control, and no BP value, baseline electrolytes, renal function or sulfa allergy check was documented before starting.
flags.consider: You might confirm office BP readings, check a basic metabolic panel and urine albumin, ask about sulfa allergy, and weigh an ACE inhibitor or ARB.

evidence.quote: i'm gon na go ahead and start you on some hydrochlorothiazide
sometimes you can have a cross reaction with some other medications like sulfa medications

flags.title: Echocardiogram for murmur with exertional chest pain?
flags.concern: Exertional chest pain with a systolic ejection murmur and ankle edema raises the question of aortic stenosis or structural heart disease, which also matters before stress testing.
flags.consider: Consider an echocardiogram before or alongside the stress test.

evidence.quote: you do have a two over six systolic ejection murmur
